name: Clean inpatient beds and rooms after discharge or transfer
summary: When a patient leaves an inpatient bed, the unit clerk records the discharge, nursing staff clear out supplies and equipment, and the bed board pages an environmental services aide to do a discharge clean: strip the bed, disinfect every surface from high to low, clean and inspect the mattress, the bathroom and the floor, change curtains where required and remake the bed. Rooms of patients on isolation precautions need extra steps, such as a sporicidal second clean for C. difficile, a wait for air changes after airborne precautions, or a UV disinfection cycle. The aide marks the bed clean so patient flow can assign it. Beds wait dirty when discharges are entered late, when the aide is busy with other jobs, and in the evening and at night when fewer aides are on shift, while admitted patients wait in the ED.

baseline.org_archetype: A not-for-profit Ontario community hospital corporation with three hospitals, about 640 inpatient beds and an emergency department at each site, on a single hospital information system with an electronic bed board.
baseline.notes: Environmental services aides work rotating 24/7 shifts with fewer aides on evenings and nights. A dedicated discharge or 'bed-turn' team is used at the large site on days and evenings; elsewhere the unit's aide fits discharge cleans between routine cleaning.

unit_of_work: one discharge or transfer clean of an inpatient bed space
trigger: A patient is discharged, transferred or dies, or isolation precautions end, and the unit clerk records it in ADT so the bed shows dirty on the bed board.
end_state: The bed space is cleaned, disinfected, made up and marked clean on the bed board; any damaged mattress or equipment is reported to maintenance.

volume.seasonality: Discharges peak on weekdays between late morning and evening and fall on weekends; more isolation cleans in winter outbreaks and in COVID-19 waves.

evidence.note: Author's estimate, same as the organisation file: about 2,300 inpatient discharges a month plus 400 to 600 internal transfers and 200 to 400 cleans when isolation ends or a patient moves into isolation.

surge.cause: Winter respiratory virus season (influenza and RSV; COVID-19 waves from 2020)

evidence.note: Winter respiratory season and outbreaks add isolation cleans and transfers; same parameters as the organisation file.
Travel, discharge clean, isolation steps and bed board updates, about 60 to 75 minutes per clean including travel. Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35) are taken from the organisation file.
Prioritising the discharge queue, redeploying aides and auditing finished rooms. Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35) are taken from the organisation file.

roles.title: Manager, support services (environmental, food, plant, security)

evidence.note: Reviews turnaround reports and audit results monthly. Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35) are taken from the organisation file.
Entering the discharge in ADT, which sets the bed dirty. Not listed among the process roles in the organisation file. Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35) are taken from the organisation file.

Clinical clearing of the bed space before the clean (supplies, equipment, body fluids). Not listed among the process roles in the organisation file. Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35) are taken from the organisation file.

systems.name: Electronic bed board and patient flow dashboard
Hospital information system (electronic patient record with ADT, order entry, results, eMAR and clinical documentation)
Email, telephone, pagers and wireless phones

steps.name: Record the discharge in ADT
steps.description: After the patient leaves the room, the inpatient unit clerk discharges or transfers the patient in ADT, which changes the bed status to dirty on the bed board. Clerks often enter discharges in batches between other tasks, so the bed can sit empty but not yet dirty on the board.

error.defect_description: Discharge not entered; EVS is never paged and the bed sits empty.

evidence.note: Unit clerks update the patient care system at discharge, which pages a cleaner (khsc_beds). Times tier C.

steps.name: Clear clinical items from the bed space
steps.description: A personal support worker or nurse removes and discards supplies, takes away IV pumps, oxygen and suction equipment, empties bedpans, commodes and suction containers, and bags or discards personal items left behind, as infection control guidance assigns these tasks to clinical staff before the cleaner arrives.

error.defect_description: Equipment or body-fluid containers left in the room; the aide must wait or work around them.

control.basis: PIDAC Best Practices for Environmental Cleaning (2018) section 10.2.1.2 division of discharge tasks between clinical staff and cleaners, adopted in hospital IPAC policy.

evidence.note: Clinical staff responsibilities at discharge are listed in section 10.2.1.2. Times tier C.

steps.name: Page an aide from the bed board
steps.description: The bed board adds the bed to the environmental services discharge queue and pages or calls the wireless phone of the aide assigned to the area, with the room's isolation status.

error.defect_description: Page goes to an aide who is off shift or on break; job not picked up.

evidence.note: Automatic paging of a discharge-team cleaner when the bed is set dirty.

steps.name: Prioritise the discharge queue
steps.description: The environmental services supervisor watches the queue of dirty beds, moves beds wanted for ED or recovery room patients to the top at the request of patient flow, and moves aides from routine cleaning to discharges when the queue builds. In the evening and at night the supervisor covers several sites by phone.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Travel to the room
steps.description: The aide finishes or pauses the current job, collects the cart and a linen bag and walks to the room, sometimes on another floor or wing. Most of the delay before a clean starts is the aide finishing other work.

evidence.note: Just under 40 minutes on average for a discharge-team cleaner to reach the bed at an Ontario teaching hospital (khsc_beds). Distribution tier C, with longer waits on evenings and nights.

steps.name: Assess the room and put on protective equipment
steps.description: The aide checks the precaution sign on the door, walks through the room to see what needs replacing and whether special supplies are needed, removes clutter, prepares fresh disinfectant, cleans hands and puts on gloves and any gown, mask or eye protection the precautions require.

error.defect_description: Precaution sign missed; wrong disinfectant or PPE used.

control.basis: Hospital IPAC policy and Occupational Health and Safety Act duties for PPE use on additional precautions.

evidence.note: Appendix 6, step 1 (assessment) and step 3 (hand hygiene and PPE). Times tier C.

steps.name: Check the air-change time and wait to enter
steps.description: After a patient on airborne precautions (tuberculosis, measles, and aerosol-generating care for COVID-19) leaves, the door stays closed with the sign up until enough air changes have cleared the room; the aide waits or goes to another job, unless the bed is urgently needed and the aide cleans in an N95 respirator.

control.basis: PIDAC environmental cleaning section 11.2 and PIDAC Routine Practices and Additional Precautions: keep the door closed until air changes clear the room or wear an N95 respirator.

evidence.note: Section 11.2 cleaning rooms on airborne precautions. The wait depends on the room's air changes per hour; times tier C.

steps.name: Strip the bed and remove waste
steps.description: The aide strips the bed, rolling sheets into the soiled linen bag without shaking them, removes and replaces waste and linen bags, checks the sharps container and changes it when three-quarters full, then changes gloves and cleans hands.

error.defect_description: Sharps injury from items left in linen.

next.condition: isolation room, soiled curtain, or hospital changes curtains at each discharge

evidence.note: Appendix 6, steps 4 and 9. Times tier C.

steps.name: Change the privacy curtain
steps.description: The aide unhooks the privacy curtain, bags it for laundry and hangs a clean one using a step stool. PIDAC added a recommendation in 2018 to change curtains after all discharges, but many hospitals changed them only for isolation rooms or when visibly soiled during this period.

control.basis: PIDAC Best Practices for Environmental Cleaning (2018) recommendation that privacy curtains be changed after all discharges.

evidence.note: PIDAC recommendation 10 (new 2018); cleaning plus curtain change took 57 minutes per isolation room at baseline in ankrum2019. The 40% share is tier C.

steps.name: Clean and disinfect surfaces and equipment
steps.description: Working from clean to dirty and high to low with a fresh disinfectant cloth for each bed space, the aide cleans the door and handles, light switches, wall-mounted dispensers, the over-bed and bedside tables, chairs, call bell, telephone and television, IV pole and other equipment left in the room, and the inside and outside of the patient locker.

error.defect_description: High-touch surfaces missed (call bell, bed rails, light switch).

evidence.note: Appendix 6, step 5. A routine daily clean takes 17 minutes for a private room and 24 for a semi-private room (remi_caem); a discharge clean adds the bed, curtain and locker. Times tier C.

steps.name: Clean the bed and inspect the mattress
steps.description: The aide cleans the top and sides of the mattress, turns it to clean the underside, checks it for cracks, holes and fluid ingress, cleans the bed frame, rails, controls, headboard, footboard and casters, and leaves the mattress to dry.

error.defect_description: Damaged mattress not noticed and left in use.

evidence.note: Appendix 6, step 6. Times tier C.

steps.name: Clean the bathroom and the floor
steps.description: The aide cleans and disinfects the sink, toilet, grab bars, shower and bedpan cleaner, changing cloths after the toilet, then dust-mops and damp-mops the room floor, putting out a wet-floor sign.

next.condition: C. difficile, VRE or CPE room

evidence.note: Appendix 6, steps 7 and 8. Times tier C.

steps.name: Apply a sporicidal second clean
steps.description: For rooms of patients with C. difficile, VRE or CPE, two aides do a second full clean of the room and bathroom with a sporicidal agent, discard and replace all paper products, soap and the toilet brush, remove the curtains and leave surfaces wet for the product's contact time.

error.defect_description: Contact time not met; spores survive.

control.basis: PIDAC Best Practices for Environmental Cleaning (2018): sporicide after each C. difficile discharge, required policies for C. difficile, VRE and CPE rooms (recommendation 85); hospitals must follow PIDAC under their IPAC accountability.

evidence.note: Section 11 C. difficile measures and Appendix 6 additions for C. difficile and VRE rooms. Two-person cleaning and times tier C.

steps.name: Run a UV disinfection cycle
steps.description: The aide wheels the ultraviolet disinfection device into the empty room, positions it for line of sight to high-touch surfaces, seals the door with a warning sign, starts the cycle and returns to move and restart it for the bathroom. The room cannot be used during the cycle.

control.basis: Manufacturer and hospital safety procedure: no one in the room during UV exposure.

evidence.note: UV disinfection follows manual cleaning at discharge only (pidac_env); waiting for the device took a median 36 minutes at baseline in ankrum2019. Use at this hospital is tier C.

steps.name: Remake the bed and restock the room
steps.description: The aide removes gloves and cleans hands, makes the bed with clean linen, replenishes gloves, hand rub, soap and paper towels, and returns cleaned equipment such as IV poles and commodes to the clean storage room.

error.defect_description: Supplies not replenished; nurses must restock before the next patient.

evidence.note: Appendix 6, steps 10 to 12. Times tier C.

steps.name: Mark the bed clean on the bed board
steps.description: The aide enters the bed's clean status on the bed board by phone code or terminal before leaving the unit, which tells patient flow the bed can be assigned and closes the cleaning job with a completion time used for turnaround reports.

error.defect_description: Bed not marked clean; it sits unassigned until the coordinator notices.

evidence.note: The cleaner marks the bed clean in the patient care system; managers are alerted when a clean takes too long (khsc_beds). Times tier C.

steps.name: Audit the finished room
steps.description: The supervisor checks a sample of finished discharge cleans with a checklist and fluorescent marker dots placed before cleaning, records which high-touch items were cleaned and gives the aide feedback; a failed room is recleaned before it is used.

control.basis: PIDAC audit and feedback recommendations and Accreditation Canada infection prevention and control standards for cleaning audits.

evidence.note: Audits with fluorescent markers and feedback are recommended (pidac_env); about a third of Canadian hospitals audited medical-surgical rooms frequently (remi_caem). Sampling rate and failure rate tier C.

steps.name: Report damaged mattress or equipment
steps.description: The aide phones or enters a work order in the maintenance system for a torn mattress, broken bed control or damaged furniture, takes a damaged mattress out of service and asks for a replacement so the bed can be used.

next.condition: reported; bed clean with replacement mattress

evidence.note: Appendix 6 step 6: replace mattresses with cracks or holes. Share and times tier C.

exceptions.name: Isolation room with sporicidal clean
exceptions.description: C. difficile, VRE or CPE rooms get a two-person sporicidal second clean, sometimes followed by UV disinfection.

exceptions.name: Airborne precautions room
exceptions.description: The room stays closed until air changes clear it before the aide can enter.

exceptions.name: Curtain change
exceptions.description: The privacy curtain is changed for isolation, soiling or by hospital policy.

exceptions.name: Audit failure
exceptions.description: An audited room fails and is recleaned.

exceptions.name: Damaged mattress
exceptions.description: A damaged mattress or bed part is reported to maintenance and replaced.

benchmarks.unit: days from patient leaving to bed marked clean
benchmarks.population: Inpatient discharge cleans, Ontario community hospital, 2019-2022

evidence.note: About 65 minutes from bed flagged to clean at an Ontario hospital with a dedicated discharge team (khsc_beds), plus 15 to 30 minutes of discharge-entry lag; isolation rooms took a median 130 minutes at baseline in ankrum2019. p50 about 100 minutes, p90 about 3.5 hours with evening and night cleans.
About 25 minutes per bed at KHSC; 57 minutes for cleaning and curtain change of an isolation room at baseline in ankrum2019.

benchmarks.unit: minutes from page to aide at bed (average)
benchmarks.population: Kingston Health Sciences Centre discharge team, 2014

evidence.note: Just under 40 minutes.
Daily clean, for comparison; discharge cleans take longer.

pain_points.description: Most of the turnaround is waiting for an aide to finish other work and reach the room, not the clean itself; evening and night shifts have fewer aides when many discharges happen.

evidence.note: About 40 of 65 minutes was the time to reach the bed.

pain_points.description: Discharges entered late in ADT leave beds empty but not on the cleaning queue.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

pain_points.description: Equipment and body-fluid containers left by clinical staff delay the aide and blur who does what.

evidence.note: PIDAC notes discharge cleaning needs close cooperation between clinical staff and cleaners.

pain_points.description: Isolation cleans take two aides and longer, plus air-change waits and UV cycles, and isolation rooms are the ones most needed for new isolated patients.

evidence.note: Isolation room turnover median 130 minutes at baseline.

pain_points.description: Canadian EVS departments were often short-staffed for the cleaning standard expected, which lengthens waits and risks missed surfaces.

evidence.note: PIDAC says Canadian EVS departments are frequently under-resourced; more than half of EVS managers reported too few staff (remi_caem).

sources.title: Best Practices for Environmental Cleaning for Prevention and Control of Infections in All Health Care Settings, 3rd Edition (April 2018 text, opened in the 2025 revised file)
sources.publisher: Public Health Ontario, Provincial Infectious Diseases Advisory Committee (PIDAC)
sources.supports: Section 10.2.1.2 and Appendix 6: split of discharge tasks between clinical staff (remove supplies, equipment, body fluids, personal articles) and cleaners; discharge clean steps (assess, PPE, strip linen, clean high to low, clean and inspect mattress, bathroom, floor, remake bed, replenish); sporicide after each C. difficile discharge; airborne rooms kept closed until enough air changes; privacy curtains changed after all discharges (new 2018 recommendation); staffing levels set from average cleaning times; audits with fluorescent markers and feedback.

sources.title: Canadian study examines hospital cleaning times
sources.supports: Canadian Association of Environmental Management survey of Canadian hospitals: routine daily clean 17 minutes for a private room, 24 for semi-private, 38 for a ward; benchmarks of 25 to 30 minutes (CDC), 14 to 16 (1985 Canadian program), 12 to 21 (ISSA); more than half of EVS managers reported too few staff to meet cleaning standards.

sources.title: Preventing gridlock: New bed notification system helping smooth patient flow
sources.supports: Ontario hospital discharge cleaning team: unit clerks update the patient care system at discharge, which pages a discharge-team cleaner; just under 40 minutes on average to reach the bed and about 25 minutes to clean, about 65 minutes in total; bed allocators assign the next patient while the bed is being cleaned and keep the ED informed.

sources.title: Reduced isolation room turnover time using Lean methodology
sources.publisher: Infection Control & Hospital Epidemiology 40(10), Cambridge University Press
sources.supports: Isolation room turnover (patient exits to end of UV disinfection) at a US paediatric hospital: median 130 minutes (range 93 to 294) at baseline and 65 after Lean changes; cleaning plus curtain change 57 minutes at baseline; 36 minutes median from end of cleaning to start of UV disinfection at baseline.

assumptions: The process covers discharge and transfer cleans of inpatient bed spaces; routine daily cleaning, ED stretcher cleaning and operating room turnover are other work.

The bed is held from the discharge entry to clean (s01, s18); the occupied minutes are split across medicine (65%) and surgical (25%) beds by expected share, so each figure is the expected minutes per case. Maternity, paediatric and mental health beds are not given a resource here because the process map lists none for this process.
A UV disinfection device is added as a resource not in the organisation file; three devices across the corporation is the author's estimate, and its use on 35% of sporicidal cleans is tier C.
PIDAC's 3rd edition (2018) text was opened in a file revised in November 2025 whose pages are still marked April 2018; only 2018 content is relied on.
The 40% curtain-change share reflects partial adoption of PIDAC's 2018 recommendation to change curtains after every discharge.
The unit clerk and personal support worker steps are included though the process map entry lists only EVS roles, because the clean cannot start until the discharge is entered and the room is cleared.

The simulated median (about 2.6 hours from the patient leaving to the bed marked clean) is above the benchmark p50 of 100 minutes. The 65-minute Kingston figure was for a dedicated day and evening discharge team measured from the page; this model adds discharge-entry lag, clinical clearing and evening and night cleans by aides who also do routine cleaning, and sums the cleaning tasks in sequence (about 45 minutes) where an experienced aide overlaps them. The gap is kept rather than shortening every task below the published cleaning procedure.
Shares of the triggers are the author's split: about 80% discharges via discharge planning, 8% isolation changes, 8% internal transfers requested through patient flow and 4% deaths.
